newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmens buy more farm machinery to reshape sector.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens buy more farm machinery to reshape sector.

text.p: U.S. company Case Corp will deliver $50 million worth of agricultural machinery to Turkmenistan, an official from the Central Asian state's national machinery leasing company said on Monday.
The Turkmenselkhozservice official said the United States Export-Import had extended a loan for the deal, which covers tractors, combine harvesters and machinery for soil cultivation.
Turkmenistan, a former Soviet republic, would partly pay off the loan with deliveries of cotton, the official said.
The government has a separate, Uneximbank-led loan to buy $99 million worth of farming equipment.
Turkmenistan is racing to resurrect its agricultural sector to achieve self-sufficiency.

Its grain harvest, a failure last year at 430,000 tonnes, is forecast to recover this year to 1.2 million tonnes. Officials predict the cotton harvest will rise to 1.2 million tonnes from last year's less than 500,000 tonnes.
Turkmenistan spent $800 million last year on grain imports, some from the West, according to official figures.
